pie: h₁regʷesyéti wĺ̥kʷons-kʷe ḱlush₁yóh₂. bʰréh₂ter spélom mluHdʰí. kʷíd kʷid wérh₁yōh₂? wĺ̥kʷōs wékʷesbʰos ne trésonti. ḱwónes toy wókʷm̥ ḱléwsonti bʰéwdʰonti-kʷe. nu poh₂imnés spélom mléwHoh₂ h₁yós ǵʰwḗrm̥ gʷʰént. h₁íd skʷdʰí wĺ̥kʷōs-kʷe h₁íd éti h₂wiséntu. wĺ̥kʷōs h₂wisté. poh₂imnés ḱwónes HeHḱéwes.
english: It is getting dark, and I hear the wolves. Tell a tale, brother! Why should I say anything? The wolves do not tremble at words. But the dogs listen to your voice and stay awake. Then I shall tell the tale of the shepherd who killed the beast. Say it, and let the wolves hear it too! Hear, wolves! The dogs of the shepherd are swift.

pie: méh₂ter moy swépnos ne gʷm̥yéti. kéh₂nmn̥ moy séngʷʰe. kʷód wéḱsi? h₂wéys kéh₂nmn̥. h₂énHos moy h₁íd kh₂nét. dʰúgh₂ter l̥gʰdʰí h₁íd-kʷe ḱlush₁yé. h₂éwey moy péh₂ura h₂éwey téḱnōy séngʷʰe. wṓkʷs toy dlukéwih₂. nu swépnos gʷm̥yéti. dlukúh₂ toy súpniyeh₂ gʷm̥yóyh₁t.
english: Mother, sleep does not come to me. Sing me a song. Which one do you want? The song of the bird. Grandmother chanted it to me. Lie down, daughter, and hear it. 'Bird, little bird, sing for my child!' Your voice is sweet. Now sleep comes. May sweet dreams come to you.

pie: kʷíd méh₂ter woyḱṓs méne h₂éwh₂osyo h₁nómn̥ h₂roh₁dʰéyonti? dʰr̥sús wiHrós h₁ést. póyḱons nos h₂éǵroybʰos h₂éǵet. h₁éy néḱus. kʷís h₁ím memóne? kéh₂nmn̥ h₁ím memóne. ḱléwos ne mért. h₁nómn̥ moy éti h₂roh₁dʰéyōnti? súHnew dʰr̥sús h₁sdʰí woyḱṓs-kʷe te gʷr̥néHonti.
english: Mother, why do the villagers speak the name of my grandfather? He was a bold warrior. He drove the enemies from our fields. But he is dead. Who remembers him? The song remembers him. Fame does not die. Will they speak my name too? Be bold, son, and the villagers will praise you.

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis Héǵrom bʰugét.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: kʷóti deywóns séne póh₂imen h₂éyeri ǵʰuHéyesi? ph₂térm̥ dyḗm méh₂term̥ dʰéǵʰōm h₁n̥gʷním-kʷe. kʷíd h₁n̥gʷním ǵʰuHéyesi? h₁n̥gʷnís wékʷesh₂ h₂élyons n̥mr̥tóns bʰéreti. h₁éy diwyṓm h₁óh₃s. h₁yód h₂élyod h₁nómn̥ wérh₁oh₂ h₁n̥gʷnís ḱléweti? ne ḱléweti. h₃reǵtéh₂ h₁nómn̥h₂ wr̥h₁dʰí. nu moy séne póh₂imen h₁nómn̥h₂ déyḱe.
english: Old shepherd, how many gods do you call upon in the morning? Father Sky, Mother Earth, and Fire. Why do you call upon Fire? Fire carries the words to the other immortals. He is the mouth of the heavenly ones. If I say another name, will Fire hear? He will not hear. Say the names straight. Then show me the names, old shepherd.

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: kʷís bʰréh₂ter h₁énos h₂nḗr déh₂newi h₁épi? h₁ésyo dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s dlukéwih₂. h₁énos h₁wesuḱléwēs. solh₂wṓs woyḱṓs h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ ǵn̥nh₃énti. kúdʰe tḱéyti? dṓm h₁ésmey ne h₁ésti. stóygʰos h₁ésyo dṓm kéh₂nmn̥-kʷe h₁ésyo mā́dsos. h₁ím nos h₂éHsh₂m̥ wédʰōmes. méh₂tēr h₁ésmey mā́dsom déh₃eti. h₁ím wédʰōmes. swésor nos spéleh₂ mléwHeti.
english: Brother, who is that man by the river? His tongue is sweet. That is Of-Goodly-Fame. All the villagers know his name. Where does he dwell? There is no house for him. The path is his house, and the song is his food. Let us bring him to our hearth. Mother will give him food. Let us bring him. He will tell us tales, sister.

pie: ǵérh₂ont moy toy h₁erkʷós h₁erkʷṓd swéh₂dyōs. nu gʷéHye. tewtéh₂ h₂wéyseti wélh₁eti-kʷe. h₁ń̥gʷney nos h₁uséwōm déh₃tor h₂wisdʰí. h₂éwh₂os moy téh₂ wékʷesh₂ h₂roh₁dʰéyet. kʷíd ǵn̥néh₃si? néwom kʷid ne ǵn̥néh₃mi. ḱHsdʰí me. nu ǵn̥h₃rós h₁ési. nu toy pedés h₁épi sísdōh₂.
english: Old man, my hymn is sweeter than your hymn. Sing, then! The people will hear and choose. 'Fire, giver of good things, hear us!' My grandfather spoke those words. What do you know? I know nothing new. Teach me. Now you are wise. Then I shall sit at your feet.

pie: ǵérh₂ont h₁erkʷósyo wékʷos léykʷoh₂? mē kʷid léykʷs. deywós solh₂wéh₂ h₂ḱh₂owsyéti. h₁yód dʰrówgʰom sékʷoh₂ kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁eti? h₁erkʷóm toy ne ḱlowséyēti. wetsṓs-kʷe toy ne h₂wéksonti. h₁yéh₂ sékʷs téh₂ sékʷoh₂. h₁íh₂ trís skʷdʰí h₁íh₂-kʷe meménesi. nu h₁n̥gʷnís méwdēti.
english: Old man, shall I leave out a word of the hymn? Leave out nothing! The god hears everything. If I say a lie, what will he do? He will not heed your hymn. And your calves will not grow. What you said, I shall say. Say them three times, and you will remember them. Then Fire will rejoice.

pie: kʷíd nókʷtm̥ ph₂wéni h₁épi dʰédʰeh₁si? wékʷesh₂ téksmi. gʷḗn h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m téksti h₁eǵóh₂ h₁erkʷóm téksmi. kʷím h₁éy gʷr̥néHeti? h₃rēǵés suHnúm gʷr̥néHeti h₁yós kh₃téws h₂éti gʷémt. h₃rḗǵs toy h₂éh₂usom déh₃eti? h₁íd déh₃eti h₁yód h₁erkʷós h₁wésus. nu téksoh₂.
english: What are you doing by the fire all night? I am weaving words. A woman weaves wool; I weave a hymn. Whom will it praise? It will praise the son of the king, who came back from the battle. Will the king give you gold? He will give it, if the hymn is good. Now let me weave!

pie: gʰóstipotey toy h₁nómn̥ dʰh₁tléh₂i gʷr̥néHm̥. kʷíd moy déh₃esi? gʷṓm toy déh₃oh₂ h₁íh₂-kʷe polh₁ú h₂mélǵos dédeh₃ti. h₁íh₂ h₁uséwih₂. h₁erkʷós moy dwóyh₁ gʷówh₁e h₂élgʷʰeti. príHe dʰr̥sús h₁ési. nu dwóyh₁ gʷówh₁e h₁áyso ḱléwos-kʷe moy dh₂pnóy ḱn̥sdʰí. h₁íd ḱénsoh₂ ḱléwos-kʷe toy ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti.
english: Host, I praised your name at the assembly. What will you give me? I shall give you a cow, and she gives much milk. She is a good one. But my hymn is worth two cows. You are bold, friend! Then take two cows, and proclaim my fame at the feast. I shall proclaim it, and your fame will be imperishable.

pie: kʷíd bʰréh₂ter gʰrémesi? wiḱpóteyey tísrn̥s nókʷtn̥s kh₂nóm h₁éy-kʷe moy péh₂urom péh₃tlom déh₃t. péh₂urom péh₃tlom. kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁esi? néwom dh₂pnóy kh₂nṓh₂. wiḱpóteys ḱḗr péh₂urom h₁ésyo-kʷe kʷid ǵʰésōr ne dédeh₃ti. tewtéh₂ sméyeti. ne gʰrémēti? gʰrémetu. h₂egʰóm h₁nómn̥ h₂óyu gʷíh₃weti.
english: Why are you angry, brother? I chanted for the chief for three nights, and he gave me a small cup. A small cup! What will you do? At the feast I shall chant something new. 'The heart of the chief is small, and his hand gives nothing.' The people will laugh. Will he not be angry? Let him be angry. A bad name lives for a lifetime.

pie: h₁n̥gʷním ǵʰuHéyes. kʷíd gʷʰédʰyesi? pótni kʷid ne gʷʰédʰyoh₂. diwyṓs me gʰéldʰōnti. kʷíh₁ gʰéldʰonti? h₂éǵroybʰos wódr̥ dédh₃n̥ti gʷéwbʰos-kʷe h₂mélǵos dédh₃n̥ti. nu n̥sméy ḱóm h₁ddʰí. h₁édoh₂ méwdōh₂-kʷe. péh₂wr̥ toy gʷʰréh₁yeti téḱneh₂-kʷe toy mudréh₂.
english: You called upon Fire. What do you ask for? I ask for nothing, mistress. The heavenly ones will pay me. How do they pay? They give water to the fields and milk to the cows. Then eat with us. I shall eat, and I shall be glad. Your fire is warm, and your children are glad.

pie: kʷíd h₂egʰéh₂ wékʷesh₂ méǵʰye h₂m̥bʰí h₂roh₁dʰéyes? séneh₂m moy h₂ówim déh₃s h₁néwn̥-kʷe toy nókʷtn̥s kh₂nóm. h₁íh₂ dóh₃r̥ h₁ést. dóh₃r̥ ne dʰl̥gʰós. gʰóstipotey kéh₂nmn̥ dʰl̥gʰós. tóm dʰl̥gʰóm gʰéldʰe ḱléwos-kʷe toy ḱénsoh₂. kʷíd wéḱsi? tísrn̥s gʷṓs h₂éh₂usosyo-kʷe péh₃tlom. dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s toy dʰr̥séwih₂.
english: Why did you speak bad words about me? You gave me an old sheep, and I chanted for you nine nights. It was a gift. A gift is not a debt. A song is a debt, lord. Pay that debt, and I shall proclaim your fame. What do you want? Three cows and a cup of gold. Your tongue is bold!

pie: dʰugh₂térn̥s moy wṓkʷs ǵr̥h₂éntih₂. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs me wiHrṓs ne ḱlowséyonti. wékʷesh₂ toy éti sweh₂dúh₂. ḱHsdʰí me. wiHrṓs gʷénh₂m̥ dh₂pnóy ḱlowséyōnti? h₂énHom moy ḱlowséyont. h₁ésyeh₂s h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm. tód h₁sónt. sddʰí pr̥h₂wóm-kʷe kéh₂nmn̥ ḱludʰí. ḱléwsoh₂.
english: Daughter, my voice is old. The young men do not heed me. Your words are still sweet. Teach me. Will the warriors heed a woman at the feast? They heeded my grandmother. Her name is famous. That is true. Sit down, and hear the first song. I am listening.

pie: h₁erkʷósyo wékʷesh₂ mérsm̥. dedwóyh₂e. téḱnom mē tréses. h₁eǵóh₂ éti mérsm̥. nu kʷíd dʰéh₁s? h₁erkʷóm pr̥h₂wṓd wékʷesos h₂éti wéwkom. deywṓs ne gʰrémont. nu h₁ím h₂éti h₂éyeri wéwkōh₂. h₁ím moy ḱósyeh₂i nékʷti trís wéwkēsi?
english: I forgot the words of the hymn. I am afraid. Do not tremble, child. I too forgot once. What did you do then? I said the hymn again from the first word. The gods did not grow angry. Then I shall say it again in the morning. Will you say it to me this night, three times?

pie: kʷíd wiḱpótis h₁wesuḱléwesey h₂éh₂usosyo péh₃tlom déh₃t? h₁wesuḱléwēs h₁ésmey ḱléwos déh₃t. ḱléwos h₂éh₂usōd méǵyos. h₂nḗr ḱléwos h₁ḗdti? ḱléwos ne h₁ḗdti. h₁ésyo suHnéwes wiḱpóteys démi h₁édn̥ti. nu kéh₂nmn̥h₂ h₁éwkoh₂ h₂ówins-kʷe ne péh₂soh₂. mógʰew h₁wesuḱléwesm̥ polh₁úh₂ yéh₁ōr ḱléwse. h₁ím ḱlowséyēsi?
english: Why did the chief give Of-Goodly-Fame a cup of gold? Of-Goodly-Fame gave him fame. Fame is greater than gold. Does a man eat fame? He does not eat fame. But his sons eat in the house of the chief. Then I shall learn songs, and I shall not herd sheep. Listen to Of-Goodly-Fame for many years, boy. Will you heed him?

pie: h₁éḱwos moy h₂élyons wént. h₁ím h₁erkʷóy gʷr̥nHdʰí. h₁éy HeHḱús? h₁éy h₂énh₁mōd HéHḱyōs. nu ḱénsoh₂. h₁éy h₂éǵrons pér drémt h₁ésyo-kʷe gʰóstipotis méwdet. médʰu moy ḱósyeh₂i nékʷti píph₃ēsi. píph₃ōh₂ ḱléwos-kʷe toy ḱénsoh₂.
english: My horse overcame the others. Praise him in a hymn! Is he swift? He is swifter than the wind. Then I shall proclaim: 'He ran through the fields, and his master rejoiced.' This night you will drink my mead. I shall drink, and I shall proclaim your fame.

pie: gʷḗn moy dʰugh₂tḗr swósyo wiHrósyo dṓm h₂éyeri h₁éyti. dh₂pnóy séngʷʰēsi? séngʷʰōh₂. kʷíd moy misdʰós? h₂éh₂usosyo péh₃tlom sweh₂dú-kʷe médʰu. nu toy dʰugh₂tréy h₂éwsosm̥ diwés dʰugh₂térm̥ ǵʰuHéyōh₂. h₁íh₂m̥ sweh₂duyéh₂h₁ wókʷh₁ gʷr̥nHdʰí gʷénh₂es-kʷe te lubʰyṓnti. dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s moy m̥lités swéh₂dyōs.
english: Woman, at dawn my daughter goes to the house of her husband. Will you recite at the feast? I shall recite. And what is my reward? A cup of gold and sweet mead. Then for your daughter I shall call upon Dawn, the daughter of Sky. Praise her with a sweet voice, and the women will love you. My tongue is sweeter than honey.

pie: gʰóstipotey toy h₁eǵóh₂ démi gʰóstis. spéleh₂ mléwHmi tewtéh₂-kʷe moy mā́dsom dédeh₃ti. gʰóstey nos priHós h₁sdʰí. kʷéh₂ wóydth₂e? káproh₁ h₁égʷʰis-kʷe spélom wóydh₂e. téḱneh₂ moy tód lubʰyéti. h₁ddʰí píph₃e-kʷe. nu nos h₁íd mluHdʰí. médʰu toy dlukú. nu th₂kéh₁yete.
english: Host, I am a guest in your house. I tell tales, and the people give me food. Be dear to us, guest! Which ones do you know? I know the tale of the goat and the serpent. My children love that one. Eat and drink! Then tell it to us. Your mead is sweet. Now be silent, all of you!

pie: kʷíd h₂énHe h₂uséy bʰéh₂si h₁yód h₁íh₂ gʷm̥sḱéti? h₂uséy bʰh₂més h₁yód h₁íh₂ gʷṓs nékʷts h₁éǵʰs wédʰeti. h₁íh₂ nos ḱlush₁yéti? ḱlush₁yéti nos. méǵʰye ḱóm h₂éyeri sth₂dʰí. h₂én stéh₂oh₂. kʷéh₂ wékʷesh₂ wéwkōh₂? wéwke diwés nos dʰúgh₂ter lukdʰí.
english: Grandmother, why do you speak to Dawn when she comes? We speak to Dawn because she leads the cows out of the night. Does she hear us? She hears us. Stand with me in the morning. I shall stand there. What words shall I say? Say: 'Daughter of Sky, shine for us!'

pie: pótni moy mā́dsom péh₂wr̥-kʷe déh₃s. kʷíd toy h₁nómn̥? h₁íd ḱénsoh₂. h₁eǵóh₂ h₁suménēs. kʷís gʰóstey túH? h₁eǵóh₂ h₂nḗr h₁yós polh₁úns h₁erkʷóns ǵn̥néh₃ti. déh₂nu pér gʷḗm. nu gʰóstey bʰh₂dʰí kéh₂ilos-kʷe te dṓm h₂wéyseti. h₁suménēs gʰostíbʰos h₁wésuh₂ dédeh₃ti. h₁ésyeh₂s ḱléwos méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t.
english: Mistress, you gave me food and fire. What is your name? I shall proclaim it. I am Kindly. And who are you, guest? I am a man who knows many hymns. I came across the river. Then speak, guest, and the whole house will hear you. 'Kindly gives good things to guests. May her fame be great!'

pie: gʰóstipotey nos kéh₂nmn̥ dh₃dʰí. wṓkʷs moy uksnés wṓkʷs. pótn̥yeh₂s moy dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s sweh₂déwih₂. nu gʷémtu méǵʰye-kʷe ḱóm píph₃e. píph₃ōh₂. pótni gʷm̥tóm gʰostéyey-kʷe nos mówdom dh₃dʰí. pótnih₂ toy m̥lités swéh₂dyōs. h₁ésyeh₂ey médʰu dh₃dʰí h₁íh₂-kʷe toy h₂élyod déh₃eti.
english: Host, give us a song! My voice is the voice of a bull. But the tongue of my wife is sweet. Then let her come, and you drink with me! I shall drink. Wife, come and give our guest joy! Your wife is sweeter than honey. Give her mead, and she will give you another.

pie: kʷíd mógʰew pr̥h₂wóm h₂usés h₁erkʷósyo wékʷos? h₁íd h₂usés h₁nómn̥. kʷíd h₁erkʷóy gʷʰédʰyomes? gʷṓs h₃épnos-kʷe gʷʰédʰyomes. h₁ím h₁éwks. nu moy h₁erkʷóm solh₂wóm wéwke. ḱúbʰra nos h₂éwsos diwés dʰúgh₂ter lukdʰí. h₃épnos nos léwkm̥-kʷe wédʰe. h₂énHe kʷid léykʷm̥? ne kʷid léykʷm̥.
english: Boy, what is the first word of the hymn of Dawn? It is the name of Dawn. And what do we ask for in the hymn? We ask for cows and wealth. You have learned it. Now say me the hymn, all of it. 'Shining Dawn, daughter of Sky, shine for us! Bring us wealth and light!' Did I leave out anything, grandmother? You left out nothing.

pie: h₂énHe h₂éǵrōs h₂susyónti. kʷóm deywóm ǵʰuHéyōmes? pérkʷunom ǵʰuHéye h₁yós h₂éḱmonm̥ gʷʰénti. kʷéh₂ wékʷesh₂ lubʰyéti? ish₁réh₂m wókʷm̥ sh₂króm-kʷe h₁erkʷóm. nu h₁ím wr̥h₁dʰí. h₂wr̥syéh₁t. pérkʷune h₂éḱmonm̥ gʷʰn̥dʰí wédōr-kʷe sh₁dʰí. nu dʰéǵʰōm péh₃eti.
english: Grandmother, the fields are dry. Which god shall we call upon? Call upon Perkunos, who strikes the stone. What words does he love? A strong voice and a holy hymn. Then say it. May it rain! 'Perkunos, strike the stone, and let the waters go!' Then the earth will drink.

pie: gʰóstipotey túH h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr. ḱḗr toy méǵh₂. ḱód péh₃tlom h₁áyso ḱléwos-kʷe moy ḱóymons pér bʰére. h₁íd bʰérōh₂ suHnéwes-kʷe moy h₁íd méǵʰye pós bʰérōnti. sh₁séni h₂éti gʷémesi? gʷémoh₂ h₁yód diwyṓs léh₁onti. príHe kéh₂ilos h₁sdʰí. n̥mr̥tṓs te stóygʰoy ph₂sih₁ént.
english: Lord, you are a giver of good things. Your heart is great. Take this cup, and carry my fame through the villages. I shall carry it, and my sons will carry it after me. Will you come back at harvest time? I shall come, if the heavenly ones allow. Be well, friend. May the immortals guard you on the path.

pie: owis, yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst, dedorḱe eḱwons wogʰom gʷr̥um wegʰontn̥s, bʰorom meǵHm, monum ōḱu bʰerontn̥s.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: kʷís te ǵérh₂ont ḱéHst? polh₁úh₂ kéh₂nmn̥h₂ wóydth₂e. méne me h₂éwh₂os ḱéHst. h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁ést. kʷíh₁ solh₂wéh₂ h₁éwks? nókʷtn̥s h₁ésyo pedsú h₁épi sísdom ḱléwsom-kʷe. pedsú toy h₁épi éti sísdōh₂? mógʰew sísde h₂ṓwsih₁-kʷe moy toy dh₃dʰí.
english: Old man, who taught you? You know many songs. My mother's father taught me. His name was famous. How did you learn all of them? I sat at his feet through the nights, and I listened. Shall I sit at your feet too? Sit, boy, and give me your ears.
